item.text:
**8B.5 Research Note**

**Positive / partial evidence**
- **Title:** Sheikh Hasina sworn in as PM for 5th term, forms 37-member cabinet  
  **Publisher:** BSS  
  **Date:** January 11, 2024  
  **URL:** https://b.bssnews.net/news-flash/167551  
  **Claim:** The cabinet included two technocrats, Yeafesh Osman and Samanta Lal Sen. That is limited but real evidence of a mixed cabinet rather than pure loyalist staffing.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.5, 8B.4, 8B.3, 8B.2

- **Title:** PM assigns charges to her 7 advisors  
  **Publisher:** The Daily Star  
  **Date:** January 21, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/pm-assigns-charges-her-7-advisors-3524926  
  **Claim:** The advisory circle included economists, academics, and a former principal secretary. That suggests some internal division of labor and administrative coordination across policy areas.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.5, 8B.4, 8B.2

- **Title:** Govt adopts plan to turn public welfare services into smart services in two years  
  **Publisher:** UNB  
  **Date:** June 4, 2024  
  **URL:** https://unb.com.bd/category/Bangladesh/govt-adopts-plan-to-turn-public-welfare-services-into-smart-services-in-two-years/136812  
  **Claim:** The government brought 52 ministries and divisions into the Smart Bangladesh implementation platform. This is the clearest whole-of-government coordination evidence I found.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.5, 8B.4, 8B.3, 8B.2, 8B.1

- **Title:** Bangladesh reaches landmark success of the Health and Gender Support Project in Cox’s Bazar  
  **Publisher:** WHO Bangladesh  
  **Date:** June 22, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.who.int/bangladesh/news/detail/22-06-2024-who-bangladesh-celebrates-landmark-success-of-the-health-and-gender-support-project-in-cox-s-bazar  
  **Claim:** The project, run through the Ministry of Health and World Bank funding, produced quantified outputs such as screenings, trained health workers, and expanded surveillance capacity. That shows coordinated execution in a vulnerable region.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.5, 8B.4, 8B.2

- **Title:** 2nd JEE Bangladesh  
  **Publisher:** WHO  
  **Date:** July 11, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.who.int/southeastasia/news/detail/11-07-2024-2nd-jee-bn  
  **Claim:** Bangladesh completed a peer-reviewed Joint External Evaluation that identified strengths, gaps, and priority actions. This is a real measurement-and-correction mechanism inside the state apparatus.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.5, 8B.4, 8B.2

- **Title:** Bangladesh receives $900 million World Bank financing to increase economic and urban resilience  
  **Publisher:** World Bank  
  **Date:** June 21, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/06/21/bangladesh-receives-900-million-world-bank-financing-to-increase-economic-and-urban-resilience-for-sustainable-growth  
  **Claim:** The package supported fiscal and financial-sector reforms, stronger banking oversight, procurement reform, and resilience spending. That is evidence of follow-through through formal institutions, not just rhetoric.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.5, 8B.4, 8B.2

- **Title:** e-GP to be made mandatory in public procurement as part of reforms  
  **Publisher:** BPPA  
  **Date:** March 6, 2024  
  **URL:** https://bppa.gov.bd/media-communication/news-1483.html  
  **Claim:** BPPA said the government was making e-GP mandatory and moving procurement onto a digital platform. That implies some real administrative discipline and enforcement across agencies.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.5, 8B.4, 8B.2

**Negative evidence**
- **Title:** Bangladesh PM Hasina secures fourth straight term in vote boycotted by main opposition  
  **Publisher:** Reuters / ThePrint  
  **Date:** January 8, 2024  
  **URL:** https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-pm-sheikh-hasina-secures-fourth-straight-term-in-vote-boycotted-by-main-opposition/1914659/  
  **Claim:** Reuters reported the BNP boycotted after Hasina refused to resign and allow a neutral authority to run the election. That suggests she would not delegate control to independent institutions when it threatened her hold on power.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.5, 8B.4, 8B.3, 8B.2, 8B.1

- **Title:** New Cabinet Formation: Loyalists, fresh faces likely to get priority  
  **Publisher:** The Daily Star  
  **Date:** January 9, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/new-cabinet-formation-loyalists-fresh-faces-likely-get-priority-3515421  
  **Claim:** Contemporaneous reporting said the new cabinet would likely prioritize loyalists and that technocrats would be rare. That points to weak meritocratic discipline and reliance on political operators.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.5, 8B.4, 8B.3, 8B.2

- **Title:** Bangladesh blocks roads and internet, deploys army to curb protests  
  **Publisher:** Reuters  
  **Date:** July 20, 2024  
  **URL:** https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-army-enforces-curfew-as-student-led-protests-spiral/2182818/  
  **Claim:** Reuters described soldiers, roadblocks, curfews, and communications shutdowns during the crackdown. This shows coercive mobilization, but not disciplined coordination for program execution.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.5, 8B.4, 8B.3

- **Title:** Bangladesh PM Hasina blames opposition for violence, curfew to remain  
  **Publisher:** Reuters / Investing.com  
  **Date:** July 22, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-pm-hasina-blames-opposition-for-violence-curfew-to-remain-3528153  
  **Claim:** Hasina kept the curfew in place and blamed political opponents for the violence. That reads as crisis control by blame-shifting rather than coordinated state discipline.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.5, 8B.4, 8B.3, 8B.2

- **Title:** Exclusive: Bangladesh army refused to suppress protest, sealing Hasina’s fate  
  **Publisher:** Reuters / VOA  
  **Date:** August 7, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.voanews.com/a/exclusive-bangladesh-army-refused-to-suppress-protest-sealing-hasina-s-fate/7733166.html  
  **Claim:** Reuters reported the army would not fire on civilians to enforce Hasina’s curfew. That is strong evidence she lacked full control over the coercive apparatus she relied on.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.5, 8B.4, 8B.3

- **Title:** Bangladesh’s internet shutdown isolates citizens, disrupts business  
  **Publisher:** Reuters / Investing.com  
  **Date:** July 26, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladeshs-internet-shutdown-isolates-citizens-disrupts-business-3539448  
  **Claim:** Reuters described a countrywide internet blackout used during the unrest, with similar controls used before elections. That shows blunt control capacity, but for suppression and regime security rather than orderly follow-through.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.5, 8B.4, 8B.3

- **Title:** Al govt created lawless economy; crony capitalism captured public organizations  
  **Publisher:** The Daily Star  
  **Date:** October 31, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/al-govt-created-lawless-economy-3741796  
  **Claim:** A white-paper lead said authoritarian practices produced crony capitalism and a nexus of politicians, bureaucrats, and business interests that captured public organizations. That is strong evidence of weak discipline and elite capture across the ruling network.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.5, 8B.4, 8B.2

**Bottom line**
- Hasina’s 2024 record shows **partial administrative coordination** in routine policy areas: Smart Bangladesh rollout, procurement digitization, some technocratic appointments, and sectoral monitoring/reform.
- The stronger pattern is **fragile control and weak cohesion under stress**: the election was tightly controlled, the July crisis exposed fractured command over the army and information space, and later commentary described patronage and elite capture.

**Search gap**
- I did not find a public 2024 source with a full internal coordination picture across ministries, party organs, regions, and security chains of command, such as cabinet minutes, implementation scorecards, or budget-execution dashboards.
- The strongest positive evidence is sectoral and procedural; the strongest negative evidence is the July crackdown and party-state fusion.
